meta.title: Burmese A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Burmese → English (see the Burmese, recall the meaning) and English → Burmese (see an English meaning, recall the Burmese). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Burmese, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 375 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — the months, Western and Burmese, time, clothes and things worn, work and jobs, relatives and the stages of life, feelings, travel, the land and the weather, animals, the body, health, food and cooking, the kitchen and the home, talking and deciding, the everyday verbs of doing, describing things and people, and the faith and the feasts — and the other 375 are the commonest remaining words of the Burmese Wikipedia. Burmese writes no spaces between words, so that text was cut into words against the dictionary, and only words of two syllables or more are taken from the count (a one-syllable count also holds every piece the cut could not place). Burmese has two registers, the written and the spoken; this deck teaches the SPOKEN one (တယ်, ရဲ့, နဲ့, ဒီ), while Wikipedia is written in the literary one (သည်, ၏, နှင့်, ဤ), whose particles are left for a later level — and its fill is encyclopaedic in places (government, history, religion). The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words met most often come first. Only words English Wiktionary has an entry for can be taught here. Every word is in the Myanmar script, as Burmese is written; the Alphabet deck, first in this collection, teaches the letters and the tone marks. Beneath each word is its pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet, as Wiktionary gives it, with the four tones marked: à low, á high, a̰ creaky, aʔ checked (short, with a catch). Many short Burmese words are several words in one spelling, so a card shows the meanings of the part of speech it teaches (ကို, the object particle; ငါး, five and fish). A noun shows the classifier it is counted with where Wiktionary names one. Example sentences are few: 119 of the 750 words have one, from Wiktionary's usage examples and from Tatoeba, which holds about 590 Burmese sentences; none is invented. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Burmese voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, pronunciation and classifiers: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Burmese Wikipedia, articles of the 2026-11-01 dump (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
